cues.zh: 你是否曾想过让自己年轻得久一点
cues.en: Have you ever wanted to stay young a little longer

cues.zh: 延缓衰老？
cues.en: and put off aging?

cues.zh: 这是人类自古以来的梦想。
cues.en: This is a dream of the ages.

cues.zh: 但长期以来，科学家们
cues.en: But scientists have for a long time

cues.zh: 都认为这根本不可能实现。
cues.en: thought this just was never going to be possible.

cues.zh: 他们认为人就是会磨损老化，对此无能为力——
cues.en: They thought you just wear out, there's nothing you can do about it --

cues.zh: 就像一只穿旧的鞋子。
cues.en: kind of like an old shoe.

cues.zh: 但如果你观察自然界，
cues.en: But if you look in nature,

cues.zh: 就会发现不同种类的动物
cues.en: you see that different kinds of animals

cues.zh: 寿命可以相差很大。
cues.en: can have really different lifespans.

cues.zh: 这些动物彼此不同，
cues.en: Now these animals are different from one another,

cues.zh: 因为它们拥有不同的基因。
cues.en: because they have different genes.

cues.zh: 这就说明
cues.en: So that suggests

cues.zh: 在这些基因中，在DNA的某个地方，
cues.en: that somewhere in these genes, somewhere in the DNA,

cues.zh: 存在着控制衰老的基因，
cues.en: are genes for aging,

cues.zh: 正是这些基因让它们的寿命各不相同。
cues.en: genes that allow them to have different lifespans.

cues.zh: 所以，既然存在这样的基因，
cues.en: So if there are genes like that,

cues.zh: 那就可以想象，
cues.en: then you can imagine that,

cues.zh: 如果在实验中能改变其中一个基因，
cues.en: if you could change one of the genes in an experiment,

cues.zh: 一个衰老基因，
cues.en: an aging gene,

cues.zh: 也许就能延缓衰老、延长寿命。
cues.en: maybe you could slow down aging and extend lifespan.

cues.zh: 如果你能做到这一点，那就能找到衰老的基因。
cues.en: And if you could do that, then you could find the genes for aging.

cues.zh: 如果这些基因存在，而且你能找到它们，
cues.en: And if they exist and you can find them,

cues.zh: 那么也许最终能对此有所作为。
cues.en: then maybe one could eventually do something about it.

cues.zh: 所以我们开始寻找控制衰老的基因。
cues.en: So we've set out to look for genes that control aging.

cues.zh: 我们没有研究这些动物。
cues.en: And we didn't study any of these animals.

cues.zh: 而是研究了一种小小的圆形线虫，叫做C. elegans，
cues.en: Instead, we studied a little, tiny, round worm called C. elegans,

cues.zh: 它大概只有一个句子中逗号那么大。
cues.en: which is just about the size of a comma in a sentence.

cues.zh: 我们当时非常乐观，觉得能发现些什么，
cues.en: And we were really optimistic that we could find something

cues.zh: 因为已有报告称存在一种长寿突变体。
cues.en: because there had been a report of a long-lived mutant.

cues.zh: 于是我们开始随机改变基因，
cues.en: So we started to change genes at random,

cues.zh: 寻找长寿的动物。
cues.en: looking for long-lived animals.

cues.zh: 我们非常幸运地发现，
cues.en: And we were very lucky to find

cues.zh: 破坏一个叫做daf-2的基因的突变
cues.en: that mutations that damage one single gene called daf-2

cues.zh: 使这种小线虫的寿命翻了一倍。
cues.en: doubled the lifespan of the little worm.

cues.zh: 你可以看到黑色部分，一个月后——
cues.en: So you can see in black, after a month --

cues.zh: 它们寿命很短；这正是我们喜欢研究它们
cues.en: they're very short-lived; that's why we like to study them

cues.zh: 来研究衰老的原因——
cues.en: for studies of aging --

cues.zh: 黑色部分，一个月后，正常的线虫全都死了。
cues.en: in black, after a month, the normal worms are all dead.

cues.zh: 但那时候，
cues.en: But at that time,

cues.zh: 大多数突变线虫还活着。
cues.en: most of the mutant worms are still alive.

cues.zh: 直到时间过去两倍，
cues.en: And it isn't until twice as long

cues.zh: 它们才全部死亡。
cues.en: that they're all dead.

cues.zh: 现在我想在这段视频里展示它们实际的样子。
cues.en: And now I want to show what they actually look like in this movie here.

cues.zh: 你们首先会看到的
cues.en: So the first thing you're going to see

cues.zh: 是正常的线虫
cues.en: is the normal worm

cues.zh: 当它处于大学生年龄——也就是年轻成年期。
cues.en: when it's about college student age -- a young adult.

cues.zh: 它是个相当可爱的小家伙。
cues.en: It's quite a cute little fellow.

cues.zh: 接下来你们会看到年轻时的长寿突变体。
cues.en: And next you're going to see the long-lived mutant when it's young.

cues.zh: 所以这只动物的寿命会是两倍长。
cues.en: So this animal is going to live twice as long.

cues.zh: 它很痛苦吗？看起来并不是。
cues.en: Is it miserable? It doesn't seem to be.

cues.zh: 它很活跃。你其实看不出区别。
cues.en: It's active. You can't tell the difference really.

cues.zh: 而且它们可以完全生育——
cues.en: And they can be completely fertile --

cues.zh: 后代数量和正常线虫一样多。
cues.en: have the same number of progeny as the normal worms do.

cues.zh: 现在把你们的手帕拿出来吧。
cues.en: Now get out your handkerchiefs here.

cues.zh: 你们会看到，仅仅两周内，
cues.en: You're going to see, in just two weeks,

cues.zh: 正常线虫就老了。
cues.en: the normal worms are old.

cues.zh: 你可以看到底部那个小脑袋在动。
cues.en: You can see the little head moving down at the bottom there.

cues.zh: 但其他部分就只是躺在那儿。
cues.en: But everything else is just lying there.

cues.zh: 这只动物显然已经进了养老院。
cues.en: The animal's clearly in the nursing home.

cues.zh: 再看看这只动物的组织，已经开始退化了。
cues.en: And if you look at the tissues of the animal, they're starting to deteriorate.

cues.zh: 即使你从没见过这种小线虫——
cues.en: You know, even if you've never seen one of these little C. elegans --

cues.zh: 你们大多数人可能都没见过——
cues.en: which probably most of you haven't seen one --

cues.zh: 你也能看出它们老了——是不是很有意思？
cues.en: you can tell they're old -- isn't that interesting?

cues.zh: 所以衰老这件事有点普遍性。
cues.en: So there's something about aging that's kind of universal.

cues.zh: 现在来看这个daf-2突变体。
cues.en: And now here is the daf-2 mutant.

cues.zh: 两万个基因里只改了一个，看看它。
cues.en: One gene is changed out of 20,000, and look at it.

cues.zh: 同样的年龄，但它没进养老院；
cues.en: It's the same age, but it's not in the nursing home;

cues.zh: 它去滑雪了。
cues.en: it's going skiing.

cues.zh: 真正酷的是：它衰老得更慢。
cues.en: This is what's really cool: it's aging more slowly.

cues.zh: 这条线虫需要两天
cues.en: It takes this worm two days

cues.zh: 才能老到正常线虫一天的程度。
cues.en: to age as much as the normal worm ages in one day.

cues.zh: 当我跟人们讲起这个，
cues.en: And when I tell people about this,

cues.zh: 他们往往会想到八九十岁的人
cues.en: they tend to think of maybe an 80 or 90 year-old person

cues.zh: 以那个年纪来说，看起来精神矍铄。
cues.en: who looks really good for being 90 or 80.

cues.zh: 但其实更像是这样：
cues.en: But it's really more like this:

cues.zh: 假设你是个三十岁的男人——或者三十多岁——
cues.en: let's say you're a 30 year-old guy -- or in your 30s --

cues.zh: 你单身，正在约会。
cues.en: and you're a bachelor and you're dating people.

cues.zh: 你遇到一个很喜欢的人，慢慢了解她。
cues.en: And you meet someone you really like, you get to know her.

cues.zh: 你们在餐厅里，你问：“你多大了？”
cues.en: And you're in a restaurant, and you say, "Well how old are you?"

cues.zh: 她说：“我60岁。”
cues.en: She says, "I'm 60."

cues.zh: 就是那种感觉。而你根本看不出来。
cues.en: That's what it's like. And you would never know.

cues.zh: 你根本不会知道，直到她告诉你。
cues.en: You would never know, until she told you.

cues.zh: （笑声）
cues.en: (Laughter)

cues.zh: 好。
cues.en: Okay.

cues.zh: 那么daf-2基因是什么呢？
cues.en: So what is the daf-2 gene?

cues.zh: 如你所知，基因是DNA的一部分，
cues.en: Well as you know, genes, which are part of the DNA,

cues.zh: 它们是制造某种蛋白质的指令。
cues.en: they're instructions to make a protein that does something.

cues.zh: 而daf-2基因
cues.en: And the daf-2 gene

cues.zh: 编码一种激素受体。
cues.en: encodes a hormone receptor.

cues.zh: 所以你在图中看到的
cues.en: So what you see in the picture there

cues.zh: 是一个细胞，红色的激素受体
cues.en: is a cell with a hormone receptor in red

cues.zh: 穿透细胞边缘。
cues.en: punching through the edge of the cell.

cues.zh: 一部分就像棒球手套。
cues.en: So part of it is like a baseball glove.

cues.zh: 一部分在外面，
cues.en: Part of it's on the outside,

cues.zh: 当激素以绿色经过时，它负责接住。
cues.en: and it's catching the hormone as it comes by in green.

cues.zh: 另一部分在里面，
cues.en: And the other part is on the inside

cues.zh: 负责把信号送进细胞。
cues.en: where it sends signals into the cell.

cues.zh: 好，那么 daf-2 受体
cues.en: Okay, so what is the daf-2 receptor

cues.zh: 在向细胞内部传达什么？
cues.en: telling the inside of the cell?

cues.zh: 我刚才说过，如果你在 daf-2 基因细胞里制造突变，
cues.en: I just told you that, if you make a mutation in the daf-2 gene cell,

cues.zh: 就会得到一个功能不那么好的受体；
cues.en: that you get a receptor that doesn't work as well;

cues.zh: 动物活得更久。
cues.en: the animal lives longer.

cues.zh: 所以这意味着这个激素受体的正常功能
cues.en: So that means that the normal function of this hormone receptor

cues.zh: 是加速衰老。
cues.en: is to speed up aging.

cues.zh: 那个箭头就是这个意思。
cues.en: That's what that arrow means.

cues.zh: 它加速衰老，让衰老进程更快。
cues.en: It speeds up aging. It makes it go faster.

cues.zh: 所以就像动物体内住着死神，
cues.en: So it's like the animal has the grim reaper inside of itself,

cues.zh: 在加速衰老。
cues.en: speeding up aging.

cues.zh: 所以这一切真的非常非常有意思。
cues.en: So this is altogether really, really interesting.

cues.zh: 它说明衰老受基因控制，
cues.en: It says that aging is subject to control by the genes,

cues.zh: 特别是受激素控制。
cues.en: and specifically by hormones.

cues.zh: 这些是什么激素？
cues.en: So what kind of hormones are these?

cues.zh: 激素有很多种，有睾酮、肾上腺素。
cues.en: There's lots of hormones. There's testosterone, adrenalin.

cues.zh: 你对其中不少都有所了解。
cues.en: You know about a lot of them.

cues.zh: 这些激素与我们体内的激素
cues.en: These hormones are similar

cues.zh: 很相似。
cues.en: to hormones that we have in our bodies.

cues.zh: daf-2激素受体
cues.en: The daf-2 hormone receptor

cues.zh: 与胰岛素和IGF-1的受体
cues.en: is very similar to the receptor

cues.zh: 非常相似。
cues.en: for the hormone insulin and IGF-1.

cues.zh: 至少胰岛素你们都听说过。
cues.en: Now you've all heard of at least insulin.

cues.zh: 胰岛素是一种激素，能促进进食后营养物质
cues.en: Insulin is a hormone that promotes the uptake of nutrients

cues.zh: 被组织吸收。
cues.en: into your tissues after you eat a meal.

cues.zh: 而IGF-1激素则促进生长。
cues.en: And the hormone IGF-1 promotes growth.

cues.zh: 这些激素的上述功能早已为人所知，
cues.en: So these functions were known for these hormones for a long time,

cues.zh: 但我们的研究表明，
cues.en: but our studies suggested

cues.zh: 它们或许还有一项无人知晓的第三功能——
cues.en: that maybe they had a third function that nobody knew about --

cues.zh: 也许它们也会影响衰老。
cues.en: maybe they also affect aging.

cues.zh: 而目前看来情况正是如此。
cues.en: And it's looking like that's the case.

cues.zh: 所以在我们用小小的秀丽隐杆线虫取得发现之后，
cues.en: So after we made our discoveries with little C. elegans,

cues.zh: 研究其他动物的人
cues.en: people who worked on other kinds of animals

cues.zh: 开始追问：如果我们在其他动物身上制造同样的daf-2突变，
cues.en: started asking, if we made the same daf-2 mutation,

cues.zh: 也就是激素受体突变，
cues.en: the hormone receptor mutation, in other animals,

cues.zh: 它们会不会活得更久？
cues.en: will they live longer?

cues.zh: 果蝇身上也是如此。
cues.en: And that is the case in flies.

cues.zh: 改变果蝇体内的这条激素通路，它们就能活得更久。
cues.en: If you change this hormone pathway in flies, they live longer.

cues.zh: 小鼠身上也一样——小鼠是和我们一样的哺乳动物。
cues.en: And also in mice -- and mice are mammals like us.

cues.zh: 所以这是一条古老的通路，
cues.en: So it's an ancient pathway,

cues.zh: 因为它必定在进化中很早就出现了，
cues.en: because it must have arisen a long time ago in evolution

cues.zh: 才能在所有这些动物身上依然起作用。
cues.en: such that it still works in all these animals.

cues.zh: 而且，共同的祖先也演化出了人类。
cues.en: And also, the common precursor also gave rise to people.

cues.zh: 所以也许它在人身上也以同样的方式起作用。
cues.en: So maybe it's working in people the same way.

cues.zh: 而且有一些线索支持这一点。
cues.en: And there are hints of this.

cues.zh: 比如，有一项研究
cues.en: So for example, there was one study that was done

cues.zh: 是在纽约市的德系犹太人群体中做的。
cues.en: in a population of Ashkenazi Jews in New York City.

cues.zh: 就像任何人群一样，
cues.en: And just like any population,

cues.zh: 大多数人活到70或80岁左右，
cues.en: most of the people live to be about 70 or 80,

cues.zh: 但有些人能活到90或100岁。
cues.en: but some live to be 90 or 100.

cues.zh: 他们发现
cues.en: And what they found

cues.zh: 活到90或100岁的人
cues.en: was that people who lived to 90 or 100

cues.zh: 更可能携带daf-2突变——
cues.en: were more likely to have daf-2 mutations --

cues.zh: 也就是基因上的改变，
cues.en: that is, changes in the gene

cues.zh: 这个基因编码IGF-1的受体。
cues.en: that encodes the receptor for IGF-1.

cues.zh: 这些改变让基因的功能不如
cues.en: And these changes made the gene not act as well

cues.zh: 正常基因那样发挥得好。
cues.en: as the normal gene would have acted.

cues.zh: 它损害了基因。
cues.en: It damaged the gene.

cues.zh: 所以这些是线索，
cues.en: So those are hints

cues.zh: 表明人类也容易受到
cues.en: suggesting that humans are susceptible

cues.zh: 衰老激素效应的影响。
cues.en: to the effects of the hormones for aging.

cues.zh: 那么下一个问题自然是：
cues.en: So the next question, of course, is:

cues.zh: 这对与年龄相关的疾病有影响吗？
cues.en: Is there any effect on age-related disease?

cues.zh: 随着年龄增长，你更容易
cues.en: As you age, you're much more likely

cues.zh: 患上癌症、阿尔茨海默病、
cues.en: to get cancer, Alzheimer's disease,

cues.zh: 心脏病，以及各种疾病。
cues.en: heart disease, all sorts of diseases.

cues.zh: 结果发现，这些长寿突变体
cues.en: It turns out that these long-lived mutants

cues.zh: 对所有这些疾病都更有抵抗力。
cues.en: are more resistant to all these diseases.

cues.zh: 它们几乎不得癌症，
cues.en: They hardly get cancer,

cues.zh: 即使得了也不那么严重。
cues.en: and when they do it's not as severe.

cues.zh: 所以这真的很有意思，某种程度上也说得通，
cues.en: So it's really interesting, and it makes sense in a way,

cues.zh: 它们还很年轻，
cues.en: that they're still young,

cues.zh: 那在变老之前怎么会得衰老相关的疾病呢？
cues.en: so why would they be getting diseases of aging until their old?

cues.zh: 所以这表明，
cues.en: So it suggests

cues.zh: 如果我们能有一种疗法或药丸
cues.en: that, if we could have a therapeutic or a pill to take

cues.zh: 在人类身上复制其中一些效果，
cues.en: to replicate some of these effects in humans,

cues.zh: 也许我们就能找到一种方法，
cues.en: maybe we would have a way

cues.zh: 同时对抗多种不同的年龄相关疾病。
cues.en: of combating lots of different age-related diseases

cues.zh: 一次性解决。
cues.en: all at once.

cues.zh: 那么激素究竟是如何影响衰老速度的呢？
cues.en: So how can a hormone ultimately affect the rate of aging?

cues.zh: 这怎么可能呢？
cues.en: How could that work?

cues.zh: 结果发现在daf-2突变体中，
cues.en: Well it turns out that in the daf-2 mutants,

cues.zh: DNA上有大量基因被开启，
cues.en: a whole lot of genes are switched on in the DNA

cues.zh: 这些基因编码保护细胞和组织的蛋白质，
cues.en: that encode proteins that protect the cells and the tissues,

cues.zh: 并修复损伤。
cues.en: and repair damage.

cues.zh: 而它们被开启的方式
cues.en: And the way that they're switched on

cues.zh: 是通过一种叫做FOXO的基因调控蛋白。
cues.en: is by a gene regulator protein called FOXO.

cues.zh: 所以在daf-2突变体中——
cues.en: So in a daf-2 mutant --

cues.zh: 你可以看到我在这里画了个X穿过受体。
cues.en: you see that I have the X drawn here through the receptor.

cues.zh: 受体运作得不太正常了。
cues.en: The receptor isn't working as well.

cues.zh: 在这种情况下，蓝色的FOXO蛋白
cues.en: Under those conditions, the FOXO protein in blue

cues.zh: 进入了细胞核——
cues.en: has gone into the nucleus --

cues.zh: 就是细胞中间那个小隔间——
cues.en: that little compartment there in the middle of the cell --

cues.zh: 它停留在基因上与之结合。
cues.en: and it's sitting down on a gene binding to it.

cues.zh: 你看到一个基因。实际上有很多基因会与FOXO结合。
cues.en: You see one gene. There are lots of genes actually that bind on FOXO.

cues.zh: 而它只是停留在其中一个上面。
cues.en: And it's just sitting on one of them.

cues.zh: 所以FOXO会开启很多基因。
cues.en: So FOXO turns on a lot of genes.

cues.zh: 它开启的基因包括抗氧化基因，
cues.en: And the genes it turns on includes antioxidant genes,

cues.zh: 我称之为“胡萝卜给予者”基因，
cues.en: genes I call carrot-giver genes,

cues.zh: 它们的蛋白质产物
cues.en: whose protein products

cues.zh: 实际上帮助其他蛋白质良好运作——
cues.en: actually help other proteins to function well --

cues.zh: 正确折叠并正确发挥功能。
cues.en: to fold correctly and function correctly.

cues.zh: 它还能护送它们到细胞的垃圾箱
cues.en: And it can also escort them to the garbage cans of the cell

cues.zh: 并在受损时回收它们。
cues.en: and recycle them if they're damaged.

cues.zh: DNA修复基因
cues.en: DNA repair genes

cues.zh: 在这些动物体内更为活跃。
cues.en: are more active in these animals.

cues.zh: 免疫系统也更加活跃。

cues.zh: 我们已证明，其中许多不同的基因

cues.en: actually contribute to the long lifespan of the daf-2 mutant.

cues.zh: 所以这真的很有趣。
cues.en: So it's really interesting.

cues.en: These animals have within them

cues.zh: 潜藏着比平常活得更久的能力。
cues.en: the latent capacity to live much longer than they normally do.

cues.en: They have the ability

cues.zh: 保护自己免受多种损伤，

cues.en: So what about the normal worm?

cues.en: Well when the daf-2 receptor is active,

cues.zh: 就会触发一系列事件，
cues.en: then it triggers a series of events

cues.zh: 阻止 FOXO

cues.en: So it can't turn the genes on.

cues.en: But what good is this for the worm?

cues.zh: 我们认为胰岛素和 IGF-1 激素
cues.en: Well we think that insulin and IGF-1 hormones

cues.zh: 是特别活跃的激素，
cues.en: are hormones that are particularly active

cues.zh: 在有利条件下——在好日子里——
cues.en: under favorable conditions -- in the good times --

cues.en: when food is plentiful and there's not a lot of stress in the environment.

cues.zh: 然后它们促进营养的吸收。
cues.en: Then they promote the uptake of nutrients.

cues.zh: 生长等等。
cues.en: grow, etc.

cues.zh: 但我们认为，在压力条件下，
cues.en: But what we think is that, under conditions of stress,

cues.zh: 这些激素的水平会下降——
cues.en: the levels of these hormones drop --

cues.zh: 比如食物供应有限时。
cues.en: for example, having limited food supply.

cues.zh: 我们认为，
cues.en: And that, we think,

cues.zh: 动物会将其识别为危险信号，
cues.en: is registered by the animal as a danger signal,

cues.zh: 一个表示情况不妙的信号，

cues.en: and that it should roll out its protective capacity.

cues.en: that improves the ability of the cell

cues.en: to protect itself and repair itself.

cues.zh: 这就是我们认为动物寿命更长的原因。
cues.en: And that's why we think the animals live longer.

cues.en: So you can think of FOXO

cues.en: as being like a building superintendent.

cues.zh: 也许他有点懒，
cues.en: So maybe he's a little bit lazy,

cues.en: but he's there, he's taking care of the building.

cues.en: But it's deteriorating.

cues.en: And then suddenly, he learns that there's going to be a hurricane.

cues.zh: 所以他本人其实什么也不干。
cues.en: So he doesn't actually do anything himself.

cues.zh: 他拿起电话——
cues.en: He gets on the telephone --

cues.zh: 就像 FOXO 前往 DNA 一样——
cues.en: just like FOXO gets on the DNA --

cues.zh: 他打电话叫来
cues.en: and he calls up

cues.zh: 屋顶工、窗户工、
cues.en: the roofer, the window person,

cues.en: the painter, the floor person.

cues.zh: 它们都会来加固房子。
cues.en: And they all come and they fortify the house.

cues.en: And then the hurricane comes through,

cues.zh: 房子的状况会比正常情况下好得多。
cues.en: and the house is in much better condition than it would normally have been in.

cues.zh: 不仅如此，它还能维持更久，
cues.en: And not only that, it can also just last longer,

cues.zh: 即使没有飓风。
cues.en: even if there isn't a hurricane.

cues.zh: 这就是我们这里的概念，
cues.en: So that's the concept here

cues.zh: 用来解释我们认为这种延长寿命的能力是如何存在的。
cues.en: for how we think this life extension ability exists.

cues.en: Now the really cool thing about FOXO

cues.en: is that there are different forms of it.

cues.en: We all have FOXO genes,

cues.en: but we don't all have exactly the same form of the FOXO gene.

cues.en: but some of us have blue eyes and some of us have brown eyes.

cues.zh: 而且有某些形式的FOXO基因
cues.en: And there are certain forms of the FOXO gene

cues.en: that have found to be more frequently present

cues.zh: 在活到90或100岁的人身上。
cues.en: in people who live to be 90 or 100.

cues.en: And that's the case all over the world,

cues.en: as you can see from these stars.

cues.en: And each one of these stars represents a population

cues.en: where scientists have asked,

cues.zh: “好吧，FOXO基因的类型是否存在差异
cues.en: "Okay, are there differences in the type of FOXO genes

cues.zh: 在那些非常长寿的人群中？”答案是存在。
cues.en: among people who live a really long time?" and there are.

cues.zh: 我们还不清楚具体机制
cues.en: We don't know the details of how this works,

cues.zh: 但我们确实知道
cues.en: but we do know then

cues.zh: FOXO基因能够影响
cues.en: that FOXO genes can impact

cues.zh: 人类的寿命。
cues.en: the lifespan of people.

cues.zh: 这意味着，也许如果我们稍作调整
cues.en: And that means that, maybe if we tweak it a little bit,

cues.zh: 就能提升人们的健康和寿命。
cues.en: we can increase the health and longevity of people.

cues.zh: 这让我非常兴奋。
cues.en: So this is really exciting to me.

cues.en: A FOXO is a protein that we found in these little, round worms

cues.zh: 发现它影响寿命
cues.en: to affect lifespan,

cues.zh: 而在这里它影响着人类的寿命。
cues.en: and here it affects lifespan in people.

cues.zh: 所以我们现在在实验室里一直尝试
cues.en: So we've been trying in our lab now

cues.zh: 开发药物
cues.en: to develop drugs

cues.zh: 来激活这个FOXO细胞
cues.en: that will activate this FOXO cell

cues.en: using human cells now

cues.en: in order to try and come up with drugs

cues.zh: 来延缓衰老和与年龄相关的疾病。
cues.en: that will delay aging and age-related diseases.

cues.zh: 我真的很乐观，这方法会奏效。
cues.en: And I'm really optimistic that this is going to work.

cues.zh: 已知有很多不同的蛋白质会影响衰老。
cues.en: There are lots of different proteins that are known to affect aging.

cues.zh: 而其中至少有一种，已经有对应的药物。
cues.en: And for at least one of them, there is a drug.

cues.en: There's one called TOR, which is another nutrient sensor,

cues.zh: 就像胰岛素通路一样。
cues.en: like the insulin pathway.

cues.en: And mutations that damage the TOR gene --

cues.zh: 就像 daf-2 突变一样——
cues.en: just like the daf-2 mutations --

cues.zh: 能延长线虫的寿命，
cues.en: extend lifespan in worms

cues.en: and flies and mice.

cues.en: even when it's pretty old, like age 60 for a human,

cues.en: that old for a mouse --

cues.en: if you give the mouse rapamycin,

cues.en: it will live longer.

cues.en: Now I don't want you all to go out taking rapamycin.

cues.en: It is a drug for people,

cues.zh: 但原因是它能抑制免疫系统。

cues.en: So people take it to prevent organ transplants from being rejected.

cues.zh: 所以这可能不是完美的药物
cues.en: So this may not be the perfect drug

cues.zh: 用来延长青春。
cues.en: for staying young longer.

cues.zh: 但即便如此，在2011年的今天，
cues.en: But still, here in the year 2011,

cues.en: there's a drug that you can give to mice at a pretty old age

cues.zh: 能延长它们的寿命，
cues.en: that will extend their lifespan,

cues.zh: 这来自这门科学
cues.en: which comes out of this science

cues.zh: 是在所有这些不同动物身上做出来的。
cues.en: that's been done in all these different animals.

cues.zh: 所以我真的很乐观，
cues.en: So I'm really optimistic,

cues.zh: 而且我觉得不会太久，我希望，
